research_updates.title: Full direct-evidence audit — Boydton/LVL campus bounded; realized and portfolio evidence separated
research_updates.notes:
COMPLETENESS MATRIX (reviewed 2026-09-06; no records request was made). Boundary/entity/address crosswalk: Microsoft Corporation is the permittee, assessor owner and agreement party. Exact searches used Microsoft, Microsoft Corporation, East Coast Data Center, Boydton, 101 Herbert Drive, 960 Herbert Drive, LVL 1-7, map 110000-02--A, PRN 38595, BN1-BN15, BN49, BN80 and phase IDs 2012-60188, 2013-84486, 2015-123227, 2015-126848 and 2018-140262. CAMA PRN 38595 and DEQ PRO-21527 support the selected contiguous Herbert Drive/LVL campus; USACE NAO-2021-01135 and Timber permit 52903-4 place Timber at Ridge Road, while the 2024 Planning Commission record places Wright Forestry parcel 132000-A-004 / PRN 3269 south of Herbert Drive. Timber, Hillcrest, Lakeside, Bishop, South Hill and other county sites therefore remain outside the selected boundary absent an authoritative parcel crosswalk.

TAX / ASSESSOR / TREASURER: Mecklenburg CAMA and Southside GIS/land-book access were searched by Microsoft Corporation, 960 Herbert Drive, PRN 38595 and map 110000-02--A; the opened PRN 38595 page supplies the 2027-2028 real-property appraisal and structure schedule. The Commissioner of Revenue pages and 2026 reassessment materials explain real- and business-personal-property administration but expose no Microsoft personal-property asset schedule. The E-Treasurer portal landing page was opened and searches used Microsoft Corporation, 101/960 Herbert Drive, PRN 38595 and the map number; the public interface requires an account number and exposes no owner/address index or downloadable bill/payment ledger. The tax-rate page supplies the $0.66-per-$100 data-center-equipment rate, but without account values, bills and receipts it cannot support selected-campus tax paid, abatement, delinquency or net revenue.

COUNTY ACCOUNTING / BOARD RECORDS: County Budget and Archive Center documents opened include FY2024-2025, FY2025-2026 and FY2026-2027 Microsoft Offsite Infrastructure Fund schedules; the May 13, 2024 Board minutes and termination agreement; the August 8, 2022 RRSA capacity agreement; and July 25, 2024 Planning Commission minutes. Agenda Center searches covered Board of Supervisors, Planning Commission and BZA materials for 2010-2026 with Microsoft, Boydton, Herbert, LVL, BN6-BN13, EIG, IDA, Fund 301 and object codes 9202/9205/9206/9207/9216. The schedules support eight LVL/Herbert expenditure components plus the two pre-existing countywide Fund 301 totals, but no public check register, ACFR schedule, invoice ledger, EIG payment history, recipient distribution, marginal service cost or campus-level reconciliation was returned. Components, receipts and expenditures are not netted or summed because scope and nesting differ.

DEVELOPMENT / INCENTIVE / COMPLIANCE: VEDP releases for the original 2010 project and six expansions through 2019 were opened, preserving announcement projections separately. Official COF tables as of December 31, 2019, December 31, 2022 and June 30, 2024 were searched by the five project IDs: the first supports four performance-date investment/job pairs marked Metrics Achieved; the 2022 table reconfirms BN7/BN8; the 2024 interim table reports BN9-BN13 company-reported progress before performance certification. JLARC RD550 page 58 supports $700,000 received for the 2015 Microsoft Mecklenburg project; RD148 evaluates the sales/use-tax exemption but withholds company-site amounts. Tobacco Commission RD41 and the FY2015 Ridge Road packet were opened; their $8.4 million aggregate, $1,152,704 recommendation and other announced grants overlap phases or lack verified payment/selected-campus allocation, so they remain source-trail facts rather than realized-cost records. County IDA/EDC and agreement searches found the EIG formula (100% tax paid, 82.5% appropriated back through the IDA until termination) but no underlying payment ledger, preventing realized local-incentive or net-fiscal claims.

PLANNING / BUILDING / LAND DISTURBANCE: The county Agenda Center, Document Center, Zoning page and Building Inspection page were searched for Microsoft Corporation, both Herbert Drive addresses, LVL 1-7, PRN 38595, BN1-BN15, East Coast Data Center, site plan, land disturbance, commercial building, certificate of occupancy and permit valuation across 2010-2026. The official sites expose forms and meeting packets but no case-level issued-permit/inspection database; searches returned the separate Wright Forestry rezoning but no selected-campus building-permit ledger, valuation, contractor list, inspection status or certificate dates. Assessor structure dates and contractor square footage are not substituted for permit valuations.

AIR / STORMWATER / EPA: Virginia DEQ's issued-air-permit indexes were searched by Microsoft, East Coast Data Center, registration 21527 and Mecklenburg and returned 21527-7 (Title V, 2024-04-24) and 21527-15 (minor NSR, 2023-09-19). The official PRO-21527 indexed text supports 165 generators in 15 buildings; direct PDF retrieval returned 403 during review, so page 2 was cross-checked in the agency index and a second extraction. EPA FRS 110042150524 was opened and cross-references EIS 17626111, ICIS-Air VA0000005111700071 and construction-stormwater VAR10P374. None publishes actual generation, runtime, fuel, emissions, discharge, violation cost, water use or economic damage; permit limits are not operating outcomes.

ELECTRICITY / TRANSMISSION: Virginia SCC transmission-project and docket searches and Dominion project materials used Microsoft, Boydton, Herbert Road Substation, Cloud Substation, Coleman Creek, Mecklenburg Electric Cooperative, DOM-2021-0009, load, tariff and interconnection for 2010-2026. The Clover-Chase City application describes an unnamed Boydton data-center-campus request above 100 MW at Cloud Sub-Coleman Creek with 156 MW projected summer load in 2026; the filing does not name Microsoft or map the load to PRN 38595 and appears tied to Cloud/Ridge-area infrastructure beyond the selected parcel. The original 2011 release's 21-MW increment is retained only as a projection. No selected-campus meter, tariff, bill, kWh, peak demand, substation cost allocation, reimbursement or current contracted capacity was found.

WATER / WASTEWATER: Searches covered RRSA, Town of Boydton, county budgets and Board attachments using Microsoft, 101/960 Herbert, LVL, tank farm, Route 58 waterline, Boydton WWTP, water user agreement, gallons, rate and bill. Recital R-7 of the 2024 termination agreement confirms private Microsoft-RRSA Water Users Agreements and payments for service, but the agreements, rates, meter volumes and bills are not attached. The August 8, 2022 county-RRSA agreement reserves 400,000 gpd for county-directed use and Fund 301 contains shared/offsite projects, neither of which allocates consumption or public cost to this campus.

WORKFORCE / PAYROLL / TRAINING: VEDP performance tables, operator impact materials, Microsoft careers/workforce pages, SVHEC annual reports and recipient stories were searched for employee, contractor, wage, payroll, Datacenter Academy, IT Academy, apprentice, internship and local hire across 2010-2026. Phase-specific VEDP job actuals and the unallocated 499-job 2023 portfolio stock are retained; the BN9-BN13 progress count is labeled interim. Microsoft's IT Academy page says 11 participants had been hired into Boydton, but gives no cohort date/denominator and is not relabeled as total employment. Live vacancies, biographies and training outcomes do not establish filled jobs, annual payroll, hours, benefits, occupation mix, residence, retention or selected-campus headcount. BLS/QCEW, Census/CBP and repository county panels are geography/industry aggregates and cannot identify Microsoft.

CONTRACTORS / SUPPLIERS / PROCUREMENT: Contractor and project searches used Microsoft Boydton, East Coast, BN6-BN13, Structure Tone, Hourigan, Lithko, TriplePoint, MEP, concrete, electrical, HVAC, vendor, subcontractor, procurement, invoice and local spend. Lithko identifies Structure Tone as customer, 350,000 square feet, nine BN6 buildings and more than 500 onsite workers; TriplePoint identifies a 515,000-square-foot multi-phase 2014 mechanical project. Mecklenburg Bids/RFPs, SAM.gov/USAspending-style federal award searches and county Fund 301 solicitations were checked using LVL, Herbert Drive, Boydton WWTP, tank farm and waterline. They do not provide a complete award/payment register, Microsoft private contract value, supplier roster, worker hours/payroll, vendor location, local purchase share or auditable construction outlay; the workforce lower bound is retained without converting it to job-years.

COMMUNITY / RECIPIENT CONFIRMATION: Microsoft Local, SVHEC 2019-2023 reports/news, SVCC/Datacenter Academy materials, county/school/library searches and named recipient searches used Boydton, Mecklenburg, grant, gift, donation, Wi-Fi, scholarship, IT Academy, Better Block, school, library and nonprofit. Direct records are limited to the $75,000 Boydton Wi-Fi contribution and recipient-side SVHEC confirmations of $45,000, $200,000 and a $24,500 network tester. The Better Block and later training-lab accounts lack recipient-side amounts; in-kind equipment and volunteer hours lack valuation. These components may overlap Microsoft's $2.7 million FY2019-FY2023 regional aggregate and are not summed.

CORPORATE / FINANCE / LEGAL: Microsoft's FY2026 SEC 10-K, SEC company filings, Virginia SCC entity/docket results, county deed/UCC/lien references, EMMA/MSRB-style municipal disclosure searches, federal court/public web indexes and county bond/TIF/IRB materials were queried for Microsoft Corporation, Boydton, Mecklenburg, East Coast Data Center, 101/960 Herbert, Industrial Development Authority, bond, revenue bond, TIF, lease, debt, lien and litigation for 2010-2026. The 10-K is global; no Boydton capex, revenue, expense, asset, debt or supplier allocation was found. No project-specific bond/TIF/IRB issuance, debt service, lien, judgment, settlement recovery or litigation-cost record surfaced; generic county performance-bond forms are not project financing.

RECORD / MODEL DECISION: The fragment contains 48 additions: 33 reported actuals and 15 source projections. Countywide taxes, jobs, community totals and Fund 301 totals stay unallocated; performance phases, interim progress, nested aggregates and grant awards are not combined. Input-output, induced, causal county-comparison and net-fiscal models remain ineligible because project-specific spending by category, annual payroll, supplier geography, tax-account reconciliation and same-scope actual public-service costs are absent.

LAST-RESORT MODEL ELIGIBILITY (policy study-modeling-policy-1.3.0, re-reviewed 2026-09-06). 1 — ACHIEVED COF INVESTMENT PHASES: REJECTED. Claims clm_study_msft_boydton_perf_2012_60188_capex, clm_study_msft_boydton_perf_2013_84486_capex, clm_study_msft_boydton_perf_2015_123227_capex and clm_study_msft_boydton_perf_2015_126848_capex are separate project IDs and performance dates marked achieved, but neither the tables nor retrieved agreements reconcile shared assets, rebasing, or overlap across expansions. A candidate sum of $676,212,147 + $610,370,818 + $824,504,900 + $688,425,394 = $2,799,513,259 is reproducible only under an unproved non-overlap assumption; distinct award IDs are necessary but not sufficient, and a max-to-sum interval would not be an evidence-bounded uncertainty range. Interim BN9-BN13 is also excluded. 2 — FY2019-FY2023 TAX NORMALIZATION: ELIGIBLE. Claim clm_study_msft_mecklenburg_property_tax_fy2019_2023 reports a single $99,000,000 portfolio cumulative amount over five named fiscal years; formula $99,000,000 / 5 = $19,800,000 per fiscal year. Scope remains Microsoft's multi-campus Mecklenburg/Southern Virginia portfolio, unallocated to the selected campus. The nested $23,000,000 2023 observation is not added or treated as a fiscal-year reconciliation. This is an average of a rounded operator report, not a current-year value or county-receipt audit. 3 — INFRASTRUCTURE ARITHMETIC / PUBLIC-COST BREAK-EVEN: PARTLY ELIGIBLE. The FY2024 LVL/Herbert claims are distinct same-year Fund 301 object-line components and sum to $19,585 + $83,256 + $1,499,983 + $33,130 + $16,893 = $1,652,847; the FY2025 components sum to $66,106 + $553,371 + $400 = $619,877. These are labeled identified-component totals only, supporting-infrastructure scope, nested in countywide Fund 301 totals, and not campus operating costs or public subsidy. Company payments, grants, countywide receipts, expenditures, carry balances and components are not netted because timing, funding incidence and nesting do not align. A separate $19,800,000-per-year same-portfolio public-service-cost break-even identity is eligible from the normalized tax contribution, but actual marginal public cost remains unobserved and no net fiscal sign is asserted. 4 — OPERATIONS HEADCOUNT: REJECTED. Achieved phase counts 30, 105, 50 and 54 occur at different performance dates; the 387 BN9-BN13 count is interim in 2024, and the 499 count is a 2023 multi-campus portfolio stock. No agreement-level employee roster or retention/concurrency crosswalk proves that any are additive; summing would mix stocks, vintages, certification statuses and scopes. 5 — RESOURCE / CONSTRUCTION SYNTHESIS: REJECTED. The 21 MW figure is an expansion projection, 165 generators is a permit equipment count without rating or runtime, and more than 500 BN6 onsite workers is an undated historical lower bound without duration, hours, payroll or spend. No project-specific meter, kWh, water volume, utilization/PUE, generator output, construction outlay, worker hours, wage, vendor location or local-purchase share bounds a defensible energy, job-year, payroll, supplier or multiplier model.

modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.

project_description: Microsoft Boydton is Microsoft Corporation’s East Coast Data Center campus at 101 and 960 Herbert Drive near Boydton in Mecklenburg County, Virginia; this account covers the contiguous Boydton/East Coast/LVL campus and excludes Microsoft’s Timber, Hillcrest, Lakeside, Bishop, and other county sites. Microsoft marked ten years of operation on August 27, 2020, while state releases document the original 2010 project and successive Boydton expansions through 2019. Virginia DEQ’s 2024 operating permit describes 165 backup engine-generator sets in 15 buildings, and county parcel PRN 38595 identifies 206.57 acres with computer-center structures built or effective from 2021 through 2024.
